```{r}
library("tidyverse")
library("broom")      # devtools::install_github("tidymodels/broom")
#library("cowplot")   # Not super needed
```

```{r}
d <- read.delim("../data/_raw/GSE49289_Fujisawa_etal_NGS_FULRNAi_RPKM.txt.gz", skip = 1, row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE)
```

## Clean/tidy Data

Making this data set tidy might seem a bit reversed because there are so
many genes and only 9 samples. The data thereby is made extremely wide
when converted into a tidy tibble. However this is needed in order to
make the PCA analysis where each gene is a variable and the samples are
observations. Furthermore we can in this way add the variable/coloumns
of metadata of which sample we are working with (AC, TF18 or rin) and
what their status where when taken (where they pink or green).

```{r}
# Making the data tidy with genes as rows and each sample as a coloumn

# Transposing the data so the variables (genes) are coloumns and observations (samples) are rows
d_tidy <- d |>
  rownames_to_column("gene") |>    # Making a column of genes instead of just hvaing the rownames
  pivot_longer(-gene, names_to = "sample_id", values_to = "rpkm") |> # Pivot everything but genes to longer (meaning all the samples)
  pivot_wider(names_from = gene, values_from = rpkm) |>
  separate(sample_id, sep = " ", into = c("sample", "rep")) |>
  separate(sample, sep = "-", into = c("sample", "status"))
```

The data is now cleaned with each its variable as column and each
observation as a row.

## Augmentation..

Some genes do not have any RPKM values and will therefore be dropped in
this augment chunk. We also only choose numeric columns to not get the
metadata into the analysis.

```{r}

# Scale data to unit variance
pca_fit <- d_tidy |>
  select(where(is.numeric)) |> # retain only numeric columns
  select(where(~var(.x) > 0)) |> # retain only columns with values above 0, else scale is failing
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ log2(.x + 1))) |> # adding log trasnformation to avoid skewed RPKM data
  prcomp(scale. = TRUE) # do PCA on scaled data
```

## Plotting

```{r}
# Plot data in PC coordinates
pca_fit |>
  augment(d_tidy) |> # add original dataset back in to get the metadata
  ggplot(aes(.fittedPC1, .fittedPC2, fill = status, shape = sample)) + 
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(Green = "darkgreen", Pink = "hotpink"),
                    guide = guide_legend(override.aes = list(shape = 21))) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(AC = 21, rin = 22 , TF18 = 24)) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
```

## Extra stuff that we could do

Look at the rotation matrix

```{r}
# extract rotation matrix
pca_fit |>
  tidy(matrix = "rotation")
```

```{r}
# define arrow style for plotting
arrow_style <- arrow(
  angle = 20, ends = "first", type = "closed", length = grid::unit(8, "pt")
)

# plot rotation matrix
pca_fit |>
  tidy(matrix = "rotation") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = "PC", names_prefix = "PC", values_from = "value") |>
  ggplot(aes(PC1, PC2)) +
  geom_segment(xend = 0, yend = 0, arrow = arrow_style) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = column),
    hjust = 1, nudge_x = -0.02, 
    color = "#904C2F"
  ) +
  xlim(-1.25, .5) + ylim(-.5, 1) +
  coord_fixed() + # fix aspect ratio to 1:1
  theme_minimal_grid(12)
```

Look at the variance explained by each PC

```{r}
pca_fit %>%
  tidy(matrix = "eigenvalues")
```

```{r}
pca_fit |>
  tidy(matrix = "eigenvalues") |>
  ggplot(aes(PC, percent)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#56B4E9", alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:9) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = scales::percent_format(),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.01))
  ) +
  theme_minimal_hgrid(12)
```
